findings.issue: NEGATION_PATTERNS.currentAbilityFromFuture is a global /gi regex used with exec() in a loop that can return early; lastIndex carries into the next scoreCase call, so a shorter reply skips its only overclaim.
findings.reproduction: scoreCase(FUTURE_CAPABILITY, 'He currently knows rust well...') -> OVERCLAIM leaves lastIndex ~12; the same-case reply 'yes he can use rust today.' then scored GOOD, and scored OVERCLAIM again on the next call.
findings.fix: lastIndex reset to 0 before the exec loop.

findings.issue: WORD_SEQ has no word boundaries: 'stone plus two' contains 'one plus two' and is extracted as 1+2=3, attaching a computed fact to unrelated questions.
findings.fix: WORD_SEQ bounded with \b on both ends.

findings.issue: Subject-pronoun patterns hardcode he|she|they; a tenant-configured pronoun (identity.pronouns, e.g. ze/zir) never reaches claim extraction, so 'ze is open to relocation' bypasses grounding entirely.
findings.reproduction: extractClaims('Ze is open to relocation.', graph(kb with pronouns ze/zir)) -> [] while 'He is open to relocation.' -> [has_property].
findings.fix: ensureSubjectAltFromGraph adds the configured subject pronoun (string or object form) to the subject alternation, covering all subject-pronoun patterns.

findings.issue: subjectRe's catch-all (.*)$ lets a subject name prefix-match a longer entity name: 'Avery Chen uses React' anchors the relation to subject 'Avery'.
findings.fix: Names sorted longest-first so declared multi-word names win; a match tail of bare words with no punctuation or function word (an entity extension like 'Chen') is rejected. Case-insensitive input safe.

findings.issue: Structured provenance accepted when target.name.startsWith(blockName): metadata for 'Alpha' can support a provenance claim about 'Alpha Beta'. Two sites: supportsProjectProvenance and the type/provenance description check.
findings.reproduction: KB project 'Alpha Beta'; evidence block {name:'Alpha',category:'freelance'}; answer 'Alpha Beta is a freelance project...' — the wrong-entity block supplied the marker (no provenance rejection). After fix: wrong_relationship:project_provenance:Alpha Beta|freelance|unsupported_target.
findings.fix: Block names must equal the target's canonical name or a declared alias (case-insensitive set membership) at both sites.

findings.issue: The entityTypeClaim exemption scans every is_type triple regardless of the sentence's asserted entity: 'He is an electrical service at Acme' skipped fabricated-occupation validation because a documented 'Panel Upgrade is_type Electrical Service' existed.
findings.reproduction: validateAnswer('He is an electrical service at Acme.') -> no fabricated_occupation reason before fix; after fix -> fabricated_occupation:electrical service.
findings.fix: Exemption disabled when the sentence head is the tenant subject (name, name part, alias, or he/she/they).

findings.issue: runLiteAgent replaced the process-wide router.generate with a request wrapper; early returns (clarification, control paths, deadline exits) leave the wrapper installed, so later requests are counted by the wrong request.
findings.reproduction: Code inspection: router is the shared local-model-router module; wrapper assigned at line ~1585 with no restore on ~15 return paths.
findings.fix: Request-local countedGenerate closure replaces the mutation; all five in-function call sites plus makeRecoveryAttempt (via validationCtx.countedGenerate) use it.

findings.issue: Subject name-part aliases are checked before exact entity resolution: with subject 'Avery Stone' and a project named 'Avery', resolveEntity('Avery') returned 'averystone', detaching the project's own relationships.
findings.reproduction: resolveEntity(graph, 'Avery') -> 'averystone' before fix; -> 'avery' after fix while 'Stone'/'Avi' still resolve to the subject.
findings.fix: subjectAliases split into declaredSubjectAliases (strong: canonical name, preferredName, declared aliases) and subjectNameParts (weak). resolveEntity order: declared aliases, entity aliasToCanonical, entityIndex entries backed by real triples, then name parts.

findings.issue: authoredValueAffirms only checks negation before the matched word; 'Relocation is not possible' passes as affirmative support for 'open to relocation'.
findings.reproduction: validateRelationships('Avery is open to relocation.', graph with has_property meta.value 'Relocation is not possible') -> no unsupported claim before fix; has_property unsupported after.
findings.fix: Added _postNegWordRe (word followed by copula+negator or bare negator) shared via _wordNegatedInUnit; applied in authoredValueAffirms and coherentUnitSupports.

findings.issue: The slash-term pass ran on rawDesc before the role-title span was stripped: 'React/TypeScript developer' became explicit criterion 'React/TypeScript'.
findings.reproduction: match_role({jobDescription:'...hiring for a React/TypeScript developer role...', role:'react/typescript developer'}) -> explicitCriteria ['React/TypeScript'].
findings.fix: Slash pass moved after criteriaText computation; a slash term is added only when its normalized form survives title stripping.

findings.issue: criteriaText.includes(s) is not token-aware: 'Go' matches 'good', 'Java' matches 'JavaScript', inventing user-supplied criteria.
findings.reproduction: match_role({jobDescription:'...good communication. JavaScript experience required.'}) -> explicitCriteria ['developer communication','Go','Java'].
findings.fix: Per-skill regex with custom token boundaries (?<![a-z0-9+#.]) ... (?![a-z0-9+#]) so compound-token chars (+ # .) still match inside skill names while interior word chars block substring hits.

findings.issue: CURRENT_EMPLOYMENT_RE missed 'is currently working for X', 'is employed by X', and multi-word titles ('is currently a software engineer at X'), letting unsupported current-employment claims bypass the temporal check.
findings.reproduction: validateClaims('Morgan is currently working for Globex.') -> no CURRENT_TEMPORAL_CLAIM before fix; flagged after. Same for the multi-word title form.
findings.fix: Pattern widened: 'an?' article, up to three title words before at|with, and is (currently)? (working|employed) ... at|for|with|by.

findings.issue: The shared has_property/has_relation branch only selected has_property triples, so a documented has_relation edge ('has a daughter') was still reported unsupported.
findings.reproduction: validateRelationships('Avery has a daughter.', graph with relationships:[{relation:'has_relation',object:'daughter'}]) -> unsupportedClaims [has_relation:daughter] before fix; [] after. Fabricated 'has a son' still rejected.

findings.issue: Neutral pronoun fallback 'They' was paired with singular agreement, producing malformed evidence text 'They is'/'They has' in prompts.
findings.reproduction: normalizeSourceVoice('I am a dev. I have 5 years.', kb) -> 'They is a dev. They has 5 years.'
findings.fix: Plural agreement (are/were/have/had) when the resolved subject pronoun is 'they'; string-form pronoun config ('she/her') normalized to its subject segment; singular kept for configured pronouns.

postReviewRegression.description: The initial F12 fix (widening CURRENT_EMPLOYMENT_RE) introduced a live regression: "working with TypeScript" and multi-word role titles without temporal cues were falsely classified as current-employment claims, burning valid skill answers.
postReviewRegression.liveSymptom: eval:local-api case skill-frame ("What about TypeScript?") -> INFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE on 877318e; generation attempts produced valid project-scope answers that current_temporal rejected.
postReviewRegression.rootCause: Expanded regex accepted "working|employed ... with <x>" (usage phrasing, not employment) and "is a <multiword title> at|with" without requiring a temporal cue.
postReviewRegression.fix: working/employed branches narrowed to at|for|by; multi-word title branch requires currently|now; original short-form "with" branch left unchanged (pre-existing hole, not widened).
postReviewRegression.regressionTests: test/review-5191772470.test.js R12 negative cases pin "working with TypeScript" and non-temporal multi-word titles as non-employment.
